claims.statement: Elastic documents service account tokens, generated by the create-service-token API or the elasticsearch-service-tokens CLI, that a service uses to authenticate with Elasticsearch as a bearer token.

sources.supports: A service account token, or service token, is a unique string that a service uses to authenticate with Elasticsearch.
To use a service account token, include the generated token value in a request with an Authorization: Bearer header.

claims.statement: Both creation methods create a service token with a guaranteed secret string length of 22; the minimal acceptable secret string length is 10, below which authentication fails. The documentation does not say how the secret string sits inside the full bearer token value.

sources.supports: Both of these methods (API and CLI) create a service token with a guaranteed secret string length of 22. The minimal, acceptable length of a secret string for a service token is 10.

claims.statement: Service tokens never expire and must be deleted to be invalidated.

sources.supports: Service tokens never expire. You must actively delete them if they are no longer needed.

openQuestions.question: The full bearer token value (encoding, prefix, total length, relation to the secret string) is not documented in the pages read; the documentation examples are truncated and no format is asserted. A source stating the encoding would be needed before any bare-value expectation.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.
